description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of different LLaMA-2 models—specifically LLaMA-2-13B and LLaMA-2-70B—on the CoLeG-E benchmark (expressed as a percentage), under varying conditions of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) applied to progressively larger datasets (D₀, D₁, D₂). The horizontal axis categorizes the models and includes a placeholder gray bar for an unspecified baseline, while the vertical axis represents CoLeG-E (%) ranging from 0 to 50 with tick marks at intervals of 10. Four distinct bar patterns correspond to different SFT conditions: light blue with diagonal stripes for “no SFT,” orange with horizontal stripes for “+ SFT on D₀,” lavender with diagonal stripes for “+ SFT on D₀, D₁,” and salmon pink with solid fill for “+ SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂.” For LLaMA-2-13B, performance increases with each additional SFT stage: from approximately 8% (no SFT) to 32% (SFT on D₀), 37% (SFT on D₀, D₁), and 39% (SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂). For LLaMA-2-70B, the trend is similar but with higher absolute performance: ~26% (no SFT), ~45% (SFT on D₀), ~50% (SFT on D₀, D₁), and ~51% (SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂). The chart visually demonstrates that both model sizes benefit from incremental SFT, with larger models achieving higher scores and diminishing returns as more data is added. The bars are grouped by model size, with each group containing four bars in ascending order of SFT complexity, and no bars are shaded or annotated beyond their pattern and position.
